name: Roofer Madness

pitch_detail.notes: ~25 ft, very thin traversing pitch right; footwork critical, fall risk onto ledge below.
Straight up the slab to the arete, finishing atop Martha's Place.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, to the mid-route ledge anchor.
rappel_detail.station: The bolted anchor at the top of pitch 2.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, to the ground. Splitting here keeps the rope from dragging.

rappels: 2 rappels from bolted anchors, breaking at the mid-route ledge to manage rope drag
descent_text: A short route typically descended by rappel or lowering directly off the bolted anchor system; the mid-route ledge anchor allows a controlled two-stage descent if needed.
approach: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to the Arlington exit, then SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington, and turn onto Squire Creek Road at the west end of town, following it to the parking area where it's gated off by washout damage. From there the approach is long and rough: hike the old roadbed past a landslide crossing (~5 minutes in), reach the original road end around 30-40 minutes from the car, then follow a faint trail through a dry streambed and alder brush, ford Squire Creek, and pick through obscure forest track before finally breaking out into the open basin roughly 2 hours from the car. This is a known bushwhacky, unmaintained approach typical of Darrington-area crags, with route-finding (flagging, cairns) required in several spots.
overview: A short, bolt-protected 2-pitch 5.11+ sport testpiece on the downhill side of the Martha's Place bivy boulder in Waterfall Basin, finishing atop the boulder.
beta: Pitch 1 (5.11+, ~25 ft) is a very thin traversing pitch where precise footwork is essential — a fall risks hitting the ledge below. Pitch 2 (5.10+) heads straight up the slab to the arete and tops out on Martha's Place. Fully bolted with 13 bolts total; the belay is split at a ledge partway up to prevent rope drag. Noted for excellent bolt placement.
